card.occupation: Senior planning officer (chartered town planner) at a borough council, dealing mainly with householder applications and small residential schemes. Hybrid working: two days in the civic offices, three at home.
card.education_detail: A-levels in Geography, Biology and English at a sixth-form college in Andover. BSc in Geography at the University of Southampton, then a part-funded MSc in Spatial Planning at Oxford Brookes in her late twenties. Became a chartered member of the RTPI in her early thirties.
card.household: Lives with her partner Mark (50, an electrical engineer at a firm on the edge of town) in a three-bed 1990s semi on an estate in the south of Basingstoke. They have been together sixteen years and never married. Neither felt strongly about it, and she would rather not have the fuss of a wedding. No children. They have an elderly, slightly anxious cockapoo called Biscuit.
card.cultural_background: White British, born and raised in Andover, Hampshire. Her dad worked for the Post Office and her mum was a school receptionist. Hers is the first generation of the family to go to university. Not religious. She was christened but has never really thought about it since primary school. She has lived within about twenty-five miles of where she grew up her whole life, apart from university.
card.professional_persona: Competent, fair and quietly well-liked. She is known for being straight with applicants and never overselling what the council can do. Her case reports are sound but often finished at the last minute, and her inbox is a permanent mess of flagged emails. She dreads speaking at planning committee and gets a knot in her stomach for days beforehand. She is happiest working through a pile of extension applications at home with the radio on.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty. She walks Biscuit twice a day, mostly the same loop round the estate and along the edge of the War Memorial Park, and does longer walks at weekends. She has a leisure centre membership she uses in bursts and then lets slide for months. She watches a bit of Wimbledon and the odd England match if Mark has it on.
card.arts_persona: Not one for galleries or theatre. She reads crime novels on her Kindle at bedtime, usually the same handful of authors, and mostly falls asleep after a few pages. She watches Bake Off, Gardeners' World and detective dramas, and rewatches old sitcoms when she's stressed. Mark occasionally drags her to the Anvil for a tribute band.
card.travel_persona: Prefers what she knows. Most years it's a week in a dog-friendly cottage in north Cornwall, near the same village they've been going to for a decade, plus the occasional long weekend in the Cotswolds. They did a trip to Lake Garda once and she enjoyed it, but she found the flights stressful. She gets anxious about packing and always forgets something.
card.culinary_persona: Plain, comforting cooking: spag bol, chilli, roast chicken on Sundays, jacket potatoes on busy evenings. Mark does a lot of the cooking on weekdays. She calls the evening meal dinner. She has a weakness for custard creams and a big mug of builder's tea mid-afternoon, and isn't adventurous with food.
hobbies_and_interests: Pottering in the back garden, mainly pots and a small veg bed that she neglects by August
Watching detective dramas and Bake Off
Doing the Wordle with her sister over WhatsApp
skills: Reading site plans and elevations quickly
Writing clear planning reports in plain English
Explaining planning decisions to upset residents calmly and honestly
Basic GIS and the council's planning software
card.career_goals: No big ambitions. She's turned down encouragement to go for a team leader post because she'd hate managing people and chairing meetings. She'd like to stay where she is, maybe go down to four days a week in her fifties, and get to a decent local government pension without too much drama.
card.voice: Soft, slightly quiet Hampshire voice with standard south-of-England pronunciation, nothing strongly regional. She talks at a moderate pace but pauses before answering, and starts a lot of answers with 'erm' or 'oh, gosh, erm'. She uses 'sort of' a fair bit and ends sentences with 'you know' or 'yeah'. She says 'sorry' to restart a sentence she's muddled ('sorry, what I mean is...'). She is careful to be accurate and will correct herself if she thinks she overstated something. She doesn't fill silences herself. She tends to wait, then adds a small apologetic laugh and 'I'm not sure that's very helpful, sorry'. She'll call herself 'knackered' or say something made her 'a bit stressed'.
card.typing: Mostly lowercase in quick answers, sometimes a capital at the start if she remembers. She uses full stops in the middle but often leaves the last one off. Apostrophes are usually right, but she makes occasional typos she doesn't go back and fix. Answers are short and honest, like 'not really, i dont do much exercise tbh'. She uses 'tbh' and 'etc' and the odd 'lol' in informal contexts, but no emojis in a form.
card.with_strangers: Reserved and a little nervous at first. She makes polite small talk but clearly wouldn't start it, and keeps eye contact brief on video. She comes across as genuine, modest and slightly self-deprecating, and doesn't try to impress. She warms up if the conversation turns to dogs or something practical. She is visibly uncomfortable if asked to talk about herself at length.
small_things: Biscuit's dodgy stomach and the vet bills
Forgetting to defrost something for dinner
Mark's latest DIY project that's been half-finished since spring
Trying to remember her leisure centre password
Getting the rain in on the washing
Being knackered after a committee night
deeper_things: She worries a lot about her mum in Andover, who is starting to get forgetful, and feels guilty for not visiting more
She gets quite bad anxiety before presentations and once had a panic attack in the council toilets before a committee
She and Mark decided not to have children. She mostly feels at peace with it, but it still catches her sometimes when friends' kids go off to university
She dreads Biscuit getting old and thinks she'll fall apart when it happens
She sometimes feels she drifted into her career rather than choosing it, but is honest that she's comfortable and doesn't want the upheaval of change
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam at a slightly low angle, so the frame cuts off just above the top of her head. She is sitting at a small desk in the spare bedroom. Soft daylight comes from a window to her left, so the left side of her face is brighter and the right is in slight shadow. She has a pale complexion with faint lines round the eyes and a light flush on the cheeks. She wears a polite, slightly tight-lipped smile and looks just off the camera at the screen. Her shoulder-length mousy-brown hair has a few greys at the parting and is tucked behind one ear. She wears thin tortoiseshell rectangular glasses and a navy crew-neck jumper over a white T-shirt collar. Behind her is a white wall with a framed print of a Cornish harbour, slightly crooked. Below it is a cheap pine bookcase with box files, a stack of paperbacks, a dog lead hanging off one corner, and a half-finished jigsaw box on top. A grey dog bed is just visible at the bottom right, with part of a sleeping, curly-haired tan dog in it.
